capabilityGaps: No direct REST DM message-by-ID retrieval, DM mutation or DM directory route was found in the current file-route inventory; absent endpoints are not counted as security denials.

The REST history peer selector resolves account usernames; account UUID, message UUID and arbitrary live nickname are not supported peer lookups, and no standalone conversation ID or sender/recipient selector is provided. before/after message IDs are scoped pagination references.

Group DM and group membership changes are unsupported. The tested ordinary event stream has no demonstrated private-DM subscription or replay surface; the tests do not claim to verify an unimplemented DM event replay/subscription. IRC CHATHISTORY/HISTSERV participant replay exists and is covered separately in matrix-dm.test.ts.

Local hibernation succeeded in the privacy test, including unauthorized edit/redaction after reconstruction. A separate mutation-fixture eviction immediately following fixture restart timed out on active workerd references (dm-gaps-results-03.json); the mutation test instead uses complete before/after stopped SQLite snapshots and independent runtime restarts, and the timed-out attempt remains preserved as infrastructure evidence.

An early search assertion mistakenly searched the server echo of the query string rather than result items and was corrected (dm-gaps-results-01.json); no production failure is inferred from that test defect.

Search correction requires actual returned public message rows and matching counts, tests unfiltered and correct-author searches, and repeats controls after restart; unsupported account UUID and conversation-ID selectors remain gaps, not successful secure-denial evidence.

evidence.testTitle: direct-message mutation ownership recipient outsider and administrator cannot edit or redact across conversations; author changes persist
evidence.scenarioScope: Recipient, outsider, administrator and wrong-peer author cannot edit an Alice/Bob message using the exercised IRC tags, while the author can.
evidence.rationale: Actual supported IRC mutation commands, independent event observers and stopped SQLite verify the named ownership boundary.
assertionDetails: Recipient Bob, outsider Charlie and rootadmin each try three supported IRC edit tags and REDACT against Alice’s message; Alice also attempts edit/redaction with an incorrect peer, and each request gets 404 or REDACT_FORBIDDEN as applicable.

Public-channel barriers prove four IRC and four event observers remain live; attempted edit text and unauthorized REDACT delivery stay absent, and event streams contain neither the private bodies nor the target message ID.
Stopped workerd SQLite direct_messages and direct_message_edits snapshots are identical before and after all rejected mutations; both other conversations remain unchanged.

Alice’s valid edit reaches Bob and persists across runtime recreation; valid redaction reaches Bob, clears/redacts stored content, survives a second recreation and leaves the unrelated Bob/Charlie and Alice/Charlie records intact.
